LESSON: READING 8.4.1 INTENSIVE READING: POETRY

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH PHYSICAL IMPAIRMENT
Strand: Strand 8
Topic 8.4: Reading 8.4.1 Intensive Reading: Poetry
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 8.4.1 Intensive Reading: Poetry, part of Strand 8 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 8 ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH PHYSICAL IMPAIRMENT.

Key inquiry question: How do you describe the characters in a poem? 2. Why are the characters in a poem important?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify inanimate characters in a given poem,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 8.4.1 Intensive Reading: Poetry in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. describe traits of inanimate characters present in a given poem,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 8.4.1 Intensive Reading: Poetry in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. appreciate the role of inanimate characters in poetry. • Find out the meaning of inanimate characters from print and digital texts, • Identify inanimate characters in a poem, • Discuss the likely inanimate characters in a poem and their traits, Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative communication modes as they share their views. • Recite a poem related to the theme using appropriate non- verbal cues, • Role-play an inanimate character in a given poem, Create a conducive environment and adequate space for learners with mobility difficulties and ensure safety for all learners as they role-play. Assign roles as per each learners’ abilities. • Relate inanimate characters with individuals in real life. 1. How do you describe the characters in a poem? 2. SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 8.4.1 Intensive Reading: Poetry together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Critical thinking as the learner makes decisions while looking for information about inanimate characters.

• Creativity and imagination as learner discusses new ways of doing things when role playing inanimate characters.

Values:
